fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into an Underwriting App
fields.features_subheading: One app takes in each submission and keeps the record of who decided what.
fields.feature_1:
Submissions read into fields

The app reads the broker's application and attachments into fields such as insured name, locations, revenue and prior carrier. Any field the AI is unsure of goes to a person.
fields.feature_2:
Referral rules written in plain English

Emergent builds each referral rule from your prompt: a limit by line of business, a class you never write, a claim count. Change a rule by prompting, and the next file follows it.
fields.feature_3:
Connected to your policy system

The app pulls policy and claim history from your policy administration system through its API and writes the outcome back. Any other tool with an API connects the same way.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts that carry a link, not the file

Slack and email alerts give the submission number and the rule that fired, with a link to the file. Applicant details stay inside the app instead of sitting in a chat thread.
fields.feature_5:
Every decision kept in a database you own

Every quote and decline is saved with the underwriter's name and stated reason, plus a timestamp. The record sits in a database you own, ready for an audit or a file review.
fields.feature_6:
Your underwriting app's code, in GitHub

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Your IT and compliance teams can read how each referral rule is written before it ever touches a live submission.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Underwriting Desks, Four Different Rules
fields.tab_content_1:
With no loss runs, S-4418 waits on the broker

Corrowdale Insurance Brokers emails Tollemarsh Underwriting Managers a liability submission for Pennycross Bistro Group, with 6 locations. The app reads it into submission S-4418 and finds the 5 years of loss runs missing. It emails the broker for them, and S-4418 waits in Zenobia Treloar's queue, marked incomplete.
fields.tab_content_2:
An $8,400,000 warehouse goes from Quentin to Ileana

Quentin Pengelly writes property risks at Dunlaverock Mutual up to $5,000,000 in total insured value. Submission S-7031, a cold-storage warehouse, comes in at $8,400,000, so the app refers it to senior underwriter Ileana Thackwell. Her alert carries only the submission number, the limit passed, and a link.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of 112 renewals, the 14 with two or more claims go to Alcina

Ingleborne Insurance has 112 commercial auto policies renewing in March. The app pulls each policy's claim count for the last three years from the claims system. The 14 policies with two or more go to underwriter Alcina Polglase for a full review. The other 98 get a renewal worksheet filled from the policy record.
fields.tab_content_4:
Rupertine opens the file when sales top $250,000

Featherstonhaugh Furniture applies to Glaister Payments for card processing, expecting $310,000 a month in card sales. Glaister reviews any application above $250,000 a month. The app reads 3 months of processing statements into application MA-2290 and emails analyst Rupertine Ombleby its number and a link.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to turn your guidelines into underwriting automation with clear referral rules, then build and test it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick one desk to start with
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the workflow in a prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Collect the rules your underwriters apply today: the classes you write and decline, each underwriter's authority limit, and the documents each line of business needs. Your underwriting manager owns this list, and every rule becomes a check the app runs or a referral it makes.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Choose a single desk, such as submission intake or renewals, and count how many files it handled last month. A narrow first build is easier to test against real outcomes, and the other desks can follow once its rules hold up.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Tell Emergent what arrives, what the app should read from it, which rules apply, and who gets each file. Emergent builds the intake screens and review queues from that description, and you change any part later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the mailbox where brokers send submissions. Then connect the system that holds your policies and claims, so that history reaches each file through its API. Rating tools and data services you already pay for connect the same way.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Agree on what an alert may show
fields.howto_step_5_des: Sit down with your compliance team and list the fields an alert is allowed to carry. A good default is the file number, the rule name, and a link. Financial and health details about an applicant stay in the app, inside the file.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Mark which outcomes the app may set by itself, such as flagging a file as incomplete, and which always wait for an underwriter, such as a quote or a decline. Each decision is saved with the name of the person who made it.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before live files arrive, replay 20 past submissions with known outcomes: clean ones, a missing document, a file over a limit, a renewal with claims. Compare each result with what your underwriters decided, and adjust the rules by prompting until they match.

faq_plan.a: Underwriting automation is software that takes in applications or submissions, reads them into structured fields, applies an underwriting team's own rules, and routes each file to the right person. The judgment calls stay with underwriters, while the software handles intake, document requests, referrals, and the record of who decided each file.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up underwriting automation?
faq_plan.a: Pick one desk first and write its rules down: which classes you accept, each person's authority limit, and the papers every line requires. Describe that desk in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder, connect the mailbox brokers use, then replay old files until the app's routing agrees with your team.

faq_plan.q: What can insurance underwriting automation handle without an underwriter?
faq_plan.a: It can handle the clerical work around each decision: reading applications into fields, checking a submission against a document list, requesting what is missing, pulling claim history, and filing everything in the right queue. Whether to accept a risk, and at what price, stays with an underwriter wherever your rules say so.

faq_plan.q: Can underwriting automation and claims handling run in one app?
faq_plan.a: Yes. An app built on Emergent can keep the submission, the bound policy, and any later claims in one database. A renewal review then reads the claim history directly. If claims is the bigger job for your team, start with insurance claims automation and add underwriting desks afterward.

faq_plan.q: Can underwriting automation approve or decline an application on its own?
faq_plan.a: It can, if you write that rule, but whether it should is a call for your underwriting and compliance teams. For insurers, the NAIC model bulletin on AI use, adopted December 4, 2023, lists the extent to which humans are involved in the final decision-making process as one consideration for an insurer's AI program.

faq_plan.q: How does underwriting automation handle a referred file that sits too long?
faq_plan.a: It sends a reminder and then escalates, on a schedule you set. For example, remind the senior underwriter after one business day and move the file to the underwriting manager after two. Emergent builds both into the app as Slack, email, or in-app alerts.

faq_plan.q: What should underwriting automation cover first?
faq_plan.a: Start with submission intake. Reading applications, checking them against a document list, and chasing missing papers takes time on every file and involves no pricing judgment. Renewals with no recent claims make a good second step, since the app can fill the worksheet and leave the sign-off to an underwriter.

faq_plan.q: How does underwriting automation handle authority limits?
faq_plan.a: It compares each file with the assigned underwriter's limit and refers anything above it to someone with a higher one. Set each ceiling as total insured value for property or a premium amount for casualty, and store the limits in a table: a promotion or a new hire then changes one row.

faq_plan.q: What should underwriting automation do when a broker never sends missing documents?
faq_plan.a: Write a rule for it before launch. For example, remind the broker after 3 business days and close the submission as incomplete after 10, with a note on the file. The broker can resubmit later, and the closed record shows when each request went out.

faq_plan.q: Can underwriting automation pull property data from outside services?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the service offers an API. The app can send a property address or a vehicle identification number to a data provider you subscribe to and save the response on the file. Emergent connects built apps to any tool with an API, and a new provider is one more connection.

plan.angle: The top results are vendor explainers and AI-underwriting software pages that define the term and list benefits. This page shows the workflow app an underwriting team builds around its own guidelines: broker submissions read into fields with missing documents chased, referrals by underwriting authority, renewals sorted by claim count, and merchant applications held for review over a volume line. Every threshold is the team's own rule, alerts carry a submission number and a link instead of applicant details, and the one regulatory fact (the NAIC model bulletin on insurers' AI use) is quoted from the NAIC text. No insurance, lending or legal advice.
